question: In a third technical round for an Oracle Server Technology campus role, the candidate was asked to **design the Snakes and Ladders game** so that when **three players play it must determine the winner**, and to **write the code** (with some follow-up optimisations). The same round then asked the candidate to **explain merge sort and write complete working code** for it. A further question gave the array `9 16 7 8 25 95 23 11` and asked which sorting algorithm would suit best and how many iterations it would take.
lookingFor: Can you identify the entities and give each one a single responsibility?
Do you model the rules cleanly (snakes, ladders, exact finish, turn order) and keep them configurable?
Can you write working, readable code under time pressure?
Do you handle edge cases such as snakes at ladder tops and overshooting 100?
Do you know merge sort well enough to explain and code it, with complexity?
followUps: How would you support multiple dice or an extra turn after a six?
How would you test the game deterministically?
Which design pattern would you use to make winning rules or dice pluggable?
Why is merge sort stable, and when would you choose quicksort or heapsort instead?
How would you detect an invalid board where snakes and ladders form an endless loop?
